1. What the data says

WhoResultSource
Indian F&O traders, FY2687.7% lost money; total loss ₹91,685 crore; average loss ~₹1.17 lakh per traderSEBI study (Sep 2026), via Open Magazine / Bajaj Broking
Indian F&O traders, FY22–2493% lost money over three years; average loss ~₹2 lakh each; total > ₹1.8 lakh croreSEBI study (Sep 2024), via Outlook Business
Indian F&O traders who lost two years running and kept going~90% lost again the next yearSEBI FY26 study
Options vs futures, FY26~88% of options traders lost vs ~66% of futures tradersSEBI FY26 study
Indian intraday cash-equity traders, FY2371% lost money; 80% lost among those with > 500 trades a year; losers paid costs equal to another 57% of their trading lossSEBI study (Jul 2024), via Business Standard / Moneylife
Brazil day traders active ≥ 300 days (2013–15)97% lost money; ~1% earned more than the minimum wageChague, De-Losso & Giovannetti, "Day Trading for a Living?"
Taiwan day traders< 1% predictably profitable after feesBarber, Lee, Liu & Odean
Indian large-cap mutual fund managers (professionals)76% lagged the index over 10 years (to Dec 2025)SPIVA India Year-End 2025

Benchmarks to beat (rough, long-run, before tax): bank FD ~6.5–7%; Nifty 50 index fund ~11–13% a year over long periods (with falls of 30–50% along the way).

2. Realistic return ranges

ApproachRealistic yearly result
Retail intraday / F&O, no tested edgeNegative for ~70–90% of people
Nifty index fund (do nothing)~11–13% long run
Professional active fund managerMost end up slightly below the index after fees
A tested, disciplined swing/positional systemIndex-like to index + a few %; the gain is often smaller drawdowns, not higher returns
Renaissance Medallion–type resultsExceptions; not a retail benchmark

My own backtests: momentum rotation and weekly pullback showed 18–27% a year, but survivorship bias inflates that — the real Nifty 200 Momentum 30 index made 14.6% a year since Oct 2020. Realistic expectation: ~12–18% a year before tax, with 15–30% drawdowns. Every intraday strategy I tested failed after costs.

3. The equation for my own yearly return

Yearly return ≈ N × E × r N = trades per year · E = average profit per trade in R (after costs) · r = % of capital risked per trade

ExampleNErYearly return
Swing, small real edge40+0.35R1%+14%
Intraday, tiny edge500+0.02R0.5%+5%
Intraday, tiny negative edge (costs)500−0.05R0.5%−12.5%

Many trades magnify a small edge both ways — costs turn a tiny edge negative, and N multiplies the loss.

4. Checklist: can I make money?

  1. Edge: does my strategy have positive expectancy after costs in a backtest on data it was not tuned on, on more than one stock list?
  2. Win rate vs break-even: is my real win rate clearly above p* = (avg loss + costs) / (avg win + avg loss)?
  3. Beat the lazy option: after costs and tax, is my return above a Nifty index fund over the same period? If not, the index fund wins.
  4. Paper trade 3–6 months (or ≥ 100 trades), then small real money; compare live results with the backtest.
  5. Size matters in ₹: 15% on ₹1 lakh is ₹15,000 a year — trading can't replace a salary on small capital.
  6. Tax (equity, India): short-term gains 20%; long-term gains 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year; intraday profit is speculative business income taxed at slab rate. A strategy that trades often pays more tax.
  7. Stop rule: if after 12 months my net return is below the index fund's, switch to the index fund.

4b. Who actually makes the money

Trading vs investing:

  • Short-term trading is zero-sum before costs: for every rupee one trader wins on a price move, another trader loses it. After brokerage, STT, GST, exchange fees and slippage it is negative-sum for the traders as a group.
  • Long-term investing is positive-sum: companies grow earnings and pay dividends, so all holders can gain together (Nifty ~11–13% a year long run). The investor earns the business's growth, not someone else's loss.

Who wins (from most to least certain):

  1. The "house" — on every trade, win or lose: brokers (brokerage), exchanges and clearing (transaction fees), government (STT, GST, stamp duty, income tax).
  2. Proprietary trading firms and foreign institutions in F&O: SEBI FY24 — prop traders made ₹33,000 crore and FPIs ₹28,000 crore gross profit, while "individuals and others" lost over ₹61,000 crore; 96–97% of those firms' profits came from algorithmic trading. Their edges: speed, market making (earning the spread), cheaper costs, better data, huge capital and risk control.
  3. Long-term investors and index-fund holders: earn the market's growth — the most reliable route for an individual.
  4. Fund managers: earn fees whether or not they beat the index.
  5. A small minority of skilled retail traders: ~7% of individual F&O traders were net profitable over FY22–24; fewer still made meaningful money.

PlatformGood forNotes

For weekly/monthly strategies (weekly pullback, momentum rotation) a simple journal is enough: write down each signal, entry, stop, exit and costs, and compare with a Nifty index fund over the same weeks.
